family: Wallex-local demand surges (premium momentum / pump continuation), long only

setup.fees: taker 0.3% each side; net = 0.997^2 * sell/buy - 1; buy = close*(1+h), sell = close*(1-h)

variants.A: premium (close/fair-1) up >= Y over k min, Wallex k-min return > 0, premium above its trailing-24h median
variants.B: Wallex k-min return >= X and (Wallex - global) k-min return >= X/2
variants.all: k-bar toman volume >= Z x trailing-24h median of k-bar volume (floor 0.25 x mean), bar i traded, >= 2 traded bars in window

setup.portfolio: 5M toman, 1M fixed per trade (no compounding), max 3 positions, 1 per market
setup.selection_rule: lag=1 (next-minute entry), IS trades >= 20, highest IS account return
setup.note_on_returns: account returns are fixed-1M-per-trade sums; values below -100% mean the account would have been wiped out

event_study.finding: After a local surge the Wallex price falls back: premium change is negative at every horizon and swamps the small positive global drift. No grid cell has positive IS net at any horizon; gross continuation is below the 0.6% fee hurdle in every IS cell.

by_product: Local surges are reliably followed by give-back (premium falls ~0.3-0.5% within 15-60 min on average). Useful for other strategies only as a SELL-into-surge exit / do-not-buy filter, not as an entry.
